subject: Service divert advisory — APAC & EU impact, immediate customer actions
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-16T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: [ACTION] EU/APAC interconnect failure — initial triage

Vanessa / team,

Quick summary from infra: a cross-cloud peering failure in the eu-west and apac regions started at ~08:20 PDT. Traffic to eu and apac region endpoints is experiencing elevated latencies and 5xx errors for affected AZs. Host-level checks show packet loss between our regional ingress and cloud provider backbone.

Immediate asks:
- Notify impacted customers with clear reroute instructions for fallback endpoints (see quick steps below).
- CS to offer hands-on assistance for customers with residency constraints.
- Infra to prepare a consolidated postmortem link and runbook by EOD.

Temporary reroute proposal (to include in customer comms): update client host header to .fallback.redwood.com or change endpoint to <model>.global-fallback.redwood.com; SDKs will also accept region override header X-Redwood-Region-Fallback.

Attachments: reroute-runbook.pdf (runbook snippets and curl examples)

I'll follow up shortly with RCA notes.

— Karthik
Head of Regional Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Nora Diaz <ops@nimbushealth.com>, Tom Li <cto@loretech.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-16T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Service divert advisory — APAC & EU impact, immediate customer actions

Nora, Tom — hi, and thanks for the quick signal this morning.

We wanted to let you know about a regional network interruption affecting our EU (eu-west) and APAC edges beginning ~08:20 PDT. Some requests routed to those edges are returning 5xx or seeing higher latencies. Our immediate objective is to keep your application online with minimal changes.

If you can make one short change now we recommend the following (lowest-risk):
1) Swap to our global fallback endpoint for the next 3–6 hours: api.redwood.com -> api.global-fallback.redwood.com
2) If you use region headers, set X-Redwood-Region-Fallback: us (or omit to allow global routing)
3) SDK users: set Redwood.config({ regionFallback: 'us' }) or call with header override.

We attached a short runbook with curl examples and a checklist: service-divert-steps.pdf (PDF). Marissa is available to walk through this with your ops team immediately.

Data residency note: requests routed to the global fallback may transit US ingress points. If your contract has strict EU-only processing, please let us know urgently — we will prioritize a dedicated channel or temporary allowance with controlled logging.

We apologize for the disruption. We will share a consolidated postmortem and any targeted compensatory credits after we finish root cause analysis.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Customer Lead, West
Redwood Inference
Attachments: service-divert-steps.pdf (PDF)

Subject: Re: Service divert advisory — APAC & EU impact, immediate customer actions

Vanessa — thanks for the heads up. We're going to flip to api.global-fallback.redwood.com now. A couple of quick Qs: 

- ETA on when eu/apac edges will be back to normal?
- Does the fallback change any rate limits or token billing behavior we should watch for?

Also, we need confirmation that no customer PII will be routed outside EU for longer than our SLA allows. If there is any risk we'll need a temporary exception workflow (and a log of requests redirected).

On it now, will confirm once our devs push the header change.

— Nora
Ops Lead

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-16T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: [INTERNAL] Root cause & interim mitigation summary (for customer follow-ups)

Team — quick summary for records and external update preparation: 

Root cause (summary): a misconfigured supplier BGP policy combined with an automated path-preference change at the cloud edge caused a short-lived partition between our eu/apac regional ingress and the provider backbone. This produced asymmetric routing and packet drops for a subset of prefixes.

Mitigations performed by 12:10 PDT:
- We pushed a targeted route override to the cloud provider for impacted prefixes.
- BGP policy reset and supplier coordination completed at 12:36 PDT.
- Health checks and gradual traffic reintroduction began 12:45 PDT.

Customer-facing points to include in postmortem:
- Impact window: 08:20 — 12:45 PDT for most traffic; residual elevated latencies until 13:00 PDT.
- Workaround: switch to api.global-fallback.redwood.com (no code changes for token/billing).
- Data residency: routed requests may transit US egress when on fallback; we kept payload logging to minimum and isolated logs per contract.
- Next steps: permanent BGP policy hardening, additional provider verification, and improved automated rollbacks.

I'll link the detailed postmortem when it's ready. Please use these bullets in customer updates; final postmortem will have timestamps and evidence.

— Karthik
Head of Regional Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
Attachment: reroute-runbook.pdf (PDF snippets)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Nora Diaz <ops@nimbushealth.com>, Tom Li <cto@loretech.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-20T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: consolidated post-incident report and next steps (Aug 16 event)

Nora, Tom — following up with the consolidated post-incident summary and actions we promised. Apologies again for the disruption.

Summary highlights:
- Impact window: Aug 16 08:20 — 12:45 PDT for most affected customers. Residual elevated latencies resolved by ~13:00 PDT.
- Root cause: supplier BGP policy mismatch + path-preference automation triggered asymmetric routing.
- What we changed: route preference hardening, automated rollback safeguards, expanded monitoring of interconnects, and a runbook update to shorten detection-to-mitigation time.

Customer remediation and support:
- We've attached the formal postmortem: postmortem-redwood-20280816.pdf
- Redwood is offering a one-time service credit equal to one day of usage for impacted paid customers; I'll work with your procurement contact if you want to pursue that.
- If you require a dedicated EU-only channel temporarily while we finalize provider attestations, we can provision that — this is a manual process and we'll scope effort after a short MAM.

Next steps for Nimbus Health:
- If you accepted the fallback, confirm you saw normal error rates and latencies after the flip (we captured notes in the mutual action plan).
- If you require the dedicated channel, reply and Marissa will create MAM items and Karthik will gate infra provisioning.

Again, sorry for the interruption — we value your trust and are committed to preventing recurrence.

Best regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Customer Lead, West
Redwood Inference
Attachments: postmortem-redwood-20280816.pdf (PDF)
